messages:
laura_infra: seeing intermittent p99 egress latency and packet drops out of east1-b since 03:10 UTC, manifests as GPU node kubelet disconnects and a trickle of pod evictions :frowning_face:

mike_sre: thanks, can you paste the node errors?

laura_infra: logs show repeated 'NetworkPlugin cni0 failed to set up' and long retries. snippet:
```
Mar 18 03:12:14 node-azb-03 kubelet[1234]: E0318 03:12:14.123 kubelet.network: failed to add network: delayed CNI Add (code=1)
Mar 18 03:12:14 node-azb-03 kubelet[1234]: eviction manager: attempting to reclaim resources
```

mike_sre: hmm, looks like the CNI agent to the local router is flapping. any recent daemonset changes?

laura_infra: no config changes in the last 24h. cloud provider reported 'partial fabric degradation' in east1-b earlier.

kevin_ops: cloud status shows a subset of ToR switches in east1-b had intermittent control-plane packet loss. they're doing partial maintenance but said they'd finish within a few hours.

ari_prod: what's the impact on customer-serving workloads? any Dedicated pools affected?

laura_infra: two Dedicated GPU pools have ~8% reduced capacity (nodes slowly evacuating). Hosted API saw tail latency spikes for a small subset of shards routed to east1-b. overall error rate +0.4% for completions.

sara_oncall: alerting: infra/eviction-east1b triggered 03:15 UTC. paging already. I'm on it.

mike_sre: propose we avoid an immediate full AZ evacuation. instead do a controlled slow-drain of the worst-hit racks while shifting traffic via smart-routing to other AZs. minimizes churn and avoids mass reboots.

ari_prod: agree on gradual approach. can Redwood routing do weighted spillover per-route?

laura_infra: yes — smart routing supports per-customer and per-model weights. we can increase other-az weight to 60% for affected shards and incrementally move.

kevin_ops: we should also ensure KV cache warmup isn't catastrophic. if we move too quickly, cold caches will spike tokens and costs. recommend 10% steps every 5m.

mike_sre: +1 to 10% steps. also set automatic fallback to region-global small-quant model if a request times out.

deploy-bot: notice: autoscaler for pool gpu-east1-b-dedicated paused scaling at 03:18 UTC due to node drain annotations.

laura_infra: tagging affected nodes with `evac-slow: true` to avoid immediate preemptions, will cordon/evict after traffic shift reaches 80% other-az.

ari_prod: feature flag ready to route per-model. triggering canary for low-volume customers first.

kevin_ops: cost note: spilling to on-demand across other AZs increases unit cost ~18% for affected requests. we should track cost delta and only keep elevated weights until stability confirmed.

mike_sre: operational playbook step: 1) set routing spill 10% -> 60% -> 80% in 10m windows 2) cordon nodes in impacted rack groups once spill >= 80% 3) monitor token/cost delta and SLOs 4) if errors persist, move to full AZ fence and evacuate.

laura_infra: executing step 1 now: routing increase to 10% other-az for shards {shard-7, shard-12, shard-14}.

sara_oncall: monitoring traces and real user latencies. currently p99 back to baseline for the canary customers. no new errors.

mike_sre: step 2 scheduled at +30m if metrics stable. what's our pod reschedule time for GPU images (with cache pulls)?

kevin_ops: image pull + startup ~1m on warm nodes, ~3-4m on cold. KV cache rebuild may add 30-90s per session.

ari_prod: can we pre-warm workers in target AZs? spin up additional warm standby containers before shifting too much traffic.

laura_infra: yes, I'll request burst capacity in other east1 AZs (east1-a and east1-c) for a 20% temp bump.

deploy-bot: notice: capacity request submitted (req-8921) to scheduler. ETA ~4m.

sara_oncall: after the 10% shift, observed token cost +3% but p99 steady. proceeding with next 20% shift in 5m per plan.

laura_infra: rolling to 30% now. cordon/evict not started yet. still waiting for confirm at 80%.

mike_sre: quick check: any nodes showing repeated GPU ECC or hardware faults or is it purely network?

laura_infra: hardware OK, all errors are network timeouts and kubelet reprobes. no disk or GPU failures.

kevin_ops: recommend enabling ephemeral fallback to quantized-4bit variants on spilled traffic to reduce token cost while caches cold. product ok with slight quality tradeoff?

ari_prod: ok for non-priority customers, gate by route. mark model variants allowed: q4_0 and q4_1.

sara_oncall: metrics: error rate stable, 99th latency improving. cost spike contained at +7% for affected minute windows.

laura_infra: reaching 80% spill now for those shards. standing by to cordon racks: rack-azb-5 and rack-azb-8.

mike_sre: cordon and evict sequence: cordon -> drain with `--grace-period=120` -> force if pods don't move in 10m -> mark nodes `fence: true` for scheduler.

laura_infra: running drain on rack-azb-5 -> evictions proceeding. one slow pod stuck on imagepull; telling scheduler to increase retries.

deploy-bot: notice: node node-azb-05 removed from pool at 03:54 UTC, pods rescheduled.

ari_prod: monitor for QoS regressions on retries. if any SLOs hit we should rollback to 60% spill and try again.

sara_oncall: no SLO breaches so far. the slow imagepull was due to transient registry throttling, resolved after retry.

kevin_ops: after draining rack-azb-5, cost delta normalized. proceed with rack-azb-8.

laura_infra: draining rack-azb-8 now. will mark nodes `evac-complete` when done.

mike_sre: good. after racks drained, open ticket to cloud provider for follow-up and request switch-level packet captures. set severity medium.

laura_infra: evac-complete for rack-azb-5, rack-azb-8. marking nodes fenced and updating inventory. moving remaining minor drains to maintenance window overnight.

ari_prod: thanks team. next steps: full postmortem if provider confirms fabric issue; update runbook with a slow-drain template.

sara_oncall: will create incident follow-up and attach timeline + metric deltas.

kevin_ops: i'll run a cost analysis for the spillover window and share in #finance.

mike_sre: nice work — graceful, controlled, minimal customer impact. :tada:
